title: Right- and left-handed parastichy directions occur about equally often

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Right- and left-handed parastichy directions occur about equally often

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Within a species, cones with a given parastichy arrangement are nearly equally divided between right-handed and left-handed spiral directions (e.g. 224 versus 243 among 467 Norway spruce cones).

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In each case they were nearly equally divided as regards direction; for instance of the 467 cones shewing the five-eight arrangement, the five-series ran in right-handed spirals in 224 cases, and in left-handed spirals in 243.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Numbers of parastichies”. Scope: conifer cones (Norway spruce) and phyllotactic systems generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a simple binomial prediction with an explicit historical benchmark. Public cone imagery should provide sufficient sample size for a decisive modern test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score handedness of a designated parastichy family in large species-stratified cone image samples and test frequencies against 0.5, including a replication of the Norway spruce 5/8 class. Strong balanced frequencies support the claim; consistent directional bias refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Image availability may be spatially and taxonomically biased.

A consistent viewing convention is needed to assign handedness.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Handedness is recorded directly in the open sunflower counts, and a binomial test of equal direction is immediate. That decides the general claim of near equality for a large, single-species sample of the same kind of spiral system. The particular spruce tally is a historical count without a public specimen table, so the spruce example is not reanalyzable, while the broader chirality claim is.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Treat the two chiralities of a parastichy system as a binomial outcome and test equality within species. Near equality is confirmed if the two directions are statistically indistinguishable, as in a recount near Thompson's 224 versus 243; a substantial and repeated excess of one handedness would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A bias in one species would not by itself describe every phyllotactic system.

The Norway spruce counts quoted in the text are not a deposited raw dataset and cannot be recomputed from the sunflower file.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Within one species, heads (or cones) carrying a given parastichy pair are split about equally between the two chiralities: the larger parastichy family runs clockwise in roughly half of specimens and anticlockwise in the other half, as in Thompson's 224 right-handed versus 243 left-handed among 467 five-eight spruce cones.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: fetch.py downloads the two spreadsheets (Dryad serves them behind a browser proof-of-work challenge; the files were obtained with headless Chrome, checksummed, and a 49 KB derived table committed under derived/). analysis.py parses the photoreviewed counts (best estimate before any parenthesised range), keeps heads whose two counts are adjacent members of the Fibonacci, Lucas, double-Fibonacci or F4 sequence, and scores a head right-handed if the larger family is clockwise. The proportion right-handed is tested against 0.5 with a two-sided exact binomial test, pooled and within each pair class; the submitter counts are analysed the same way as a replication.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. In the Turing's Sunflowers data (Helianthus annuus), restrict to heads with both a clockwise and an anticlockwise parastichy count that together form an adjacent pair of one Fibonacci-type sequence (Fibonacci, Lucas, double Fibonacci or F4, as defined by Swinton et al. 2016). Define a head as right-handed when its larger family is clockwise. Pooled over all such heads, the proportion p of right-handed heads must satisfy |p - 0.5| <= 0.10 and a two-sided exact binomial test against 0.5 must give P >= 0.05. In addition, in each pair class with n >= 20 heads, |p - 0.5| <= 0.15 or the binomial P >= 0.05. Primary counts are the photoreviewed counts (author's annotation file); the submitter counts are a secondary replication.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Pooled |p - 0.5| > 0.10 with two-sided exact binomial P < 0.01 (a substantial and significant excess of one chirality), or the same pattern in the two most frequent pair classes. Any other outcome is 'mixed' (e.g. a small but significant bias with |p - 0.5| <= 0.10) or 'inconclusive' (fewer than 100 usable heads: underpowered).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: proportion of heads whose larger parastichy family runs clockwise (photoreviewed counts)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's 'direction' of the five-series (right- versus left-handed spiral) is mapped to the chirality of the larger parastichy family of a Fibonacci-type pair, scored as clockwise or anticlockwise in a fixed viewing convention (the seed face of the head as photographed). Thompson's own counts are of Norway spruce cones; no public per-cone table of those counts exists, so the test is a replication in another phyllotactic system (sunflower capitula), which the claim explicitly extends to ('phyllotactic systems generally'). Thompson's own 224:243 split is reported alongside for comparison but is not used as data.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Data from: Novel Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in the sunflower: results of a citizen science experiment (Turing's Sunflowers)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The test is on sunflower capitula, not on the Norway spruce cones Thompson cites; his spruce tally is not available as a per-cone dataset and was not re-analysed.

The sample is a citizen-science collection of mostly one cultivated species grown in many gardens; counts are subjective, but handedness (which family is larger and which way it runs) is robust to small count errors.

Heads whose two counts did not form an adjacent Fibonacci-type pair (about 40% of photoreviewed heads with two counts) were excluded by the pre-registered rule; chirality in disordered heads is not tested.

The 21/34 class (n = 29) leans right-handed (20:9, P = 0.06); it passes the pre-registered class rule only through its P value, and the two large classes lean in opposite directions, consistent with chance.

The pass criterion tolerates a true bias of up to 10 percentage points; the 95% CI (0.465-0.586) excludes biases larger than about 9 points in either direction.

fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis
